draft.title: The age of criminal responsibility
card: The age of criminal responsibility is the age at which a child can be held responsible for a crime. In NSW it is 10.
a child cannot be charged with a crime. The law treats them as unable to commit one, whatever they did.
a child can be charged, but doli incapax applies. The child is presumed unable to know the act was seriously wrong.
To overcome this, the prosecution must prove the child knew the act was seriously wrong, not just naughty. This is in addition to proving the offence itself.
draft.remember: Under 10 is never charged. At 10 to 13 the prosecution must also prove the child knew the act was seriously wrong.

a.q: How does NSW law treat a 12-year-old accused of theft?
opts: The prosecution must also prove the child knew it was wrong
The child cannot be charged because they are under 14
The child is presumed to know it was wrong, so no more proof
The child must prove they did not know it was seriously wrong
a.why: At 12 a child can be charged, but doli incapax means the prosecution must also prove the child knew the act was seriously wrong. The option saying a child under 14 cannot be charged is tempting, but the bar on charging applies only under 10.
a.clue: Think about what the prosecution must prove for ages 10 to 13.

b.q: Ethan is 9 and Priya is 13. Each takes a bike from a shed in Bathurst. Which statement is correct?
opts: Ethan cannot be charged, but Priya can if her knowledge is proved
Both can be charged if the prosecution proves the theft
Neither can be charged, as both are under 14
Ethan can be charged if he knew it was wrong, but Priya cannot
b.why: Ethan is under 10, so he cannot be charged whatever he knew. Priya is 13, so she can be charged, but only if the prosecution proves she knew the act was seriously wrong. Doli incapax does not matter for Ethan, as the age bar already applies.
b.clue: Check which age group each child falls in, then what each group needs.

proposal.title: The age of criminal responsibility
card: The age of criminal responsibility is the age at which a child can be held responsible for a crime. In NSW it is 10.
a child cannot be charged with a crime. The law treats them as unable to commit one, whatever they did.
a child can be charged, but doli incapax applies. The child is presumed not to know the act was seriously wrong.
To convict, the prosecution must overcome this by proving the child knew the act was seriously wrong, not just naughty. This is on top of proving the offence itself.
proposal.remember: Under 10: no charge. Aged 10 to 13: a charge is possible, but a conviction needs proof the child knew the act was seriously wrong.

a.q: A 12-year-old is charged with theft in NSW. What else must be shown for a conviction?
opts: That the child knew the act was seriously wrong
That the child knew the act was naughty or mischievous
Nothing more, as the child is aged 10 or over
That the child is mature enough to be tried as an adult
a.why: At 12, doli incapax applies, so the prosecution must prove the child knew the act was seriously wrong, on top of proving the theft. Knowing it was naughty or mischievous is tempting, but that is not enough to overcome the presumption.
a.clue: Reread what doli incapax presumes about a child of 12.

b.q: Ethan is 9 and Priya is 13. Each takes a bike from a shed in Bathurst. Which statement is correct?
opts: Only Priya can be charged, but doli incapax applies to her
Both can be charged, and doli incapax applies to both
Neither can be charged, as both are under 14
Only Priya can be charged, and doli incapax does not apply
b.why: Ethan is under 10, so he cannot be charged whatever he knew. Priya is 13, which is still in the 10 to 13 group, so she can be charged, but to convict her the prosecution must prove she knew the act was seriously wrong. Thinking 13 is too old for doli incapax is the tempting mistake.
b.clue: Is 13 inside or outside the 10 to 13 group?
